candidates.title: Continuous Hand Movement Dataset for Daily Living Activities using MediaPipe
candidates.description: This dataset presents a continuous hand joint angle time-series dataset collected using a monocular RGB webcam and the MediaPipe Hands framework, designed to support research in human motion analysis, grasp recognition, biomechanics, and time-series forecasting. Motivation Understanding human hand movement is critical for a wide range of applications including human-computer interaction (HCI), robotics, rehabilitation systems, and assistive technologies. While several datasets exist for gesture recognition, most are limited to discrete gestures or image-based classification tasks. In contrast, this dataset focuses on continuous temporal dynamics of hand motion, enabling the development of models for sequence prediction, temporal segmentation, and motion forecasting. Data Collection Setup The dataset was collected using: A monocular RGB webcam The MediaPipe Hands framework for real-time hand landmark detection From the detected 3D landmarks, 11 anatomically meaningful joint angles were computed per frame using geometric relationships between landmark points. The dataset is recorded in a real-world environment, without specialized motion capture systems, making it highly relevant for practical AI applications. Dataset Structure The dataset includes recordings from: 10 right-handed subjects Each subject performs multiple sessions, where: Each session is recorded as a single continuous time-series Sessions include multiple trials and grip executions Temporal annotations are provided via: Trial_ID (trial segmentation) Grip_ID (grasp type segmentation) Joint Angle Features (11) The following joint angles are computed: Thumb_CMC Thumb_MCP Thumb_IP Index_MCP Index_PIP Middle_MCP Middle_PIP Ring_MCP Ring_PIP Little_MCP Little_PIP All angles are measured in degrees. Grip Types and Activities The dataset includes five common daily living grasp patterns: Power Grasp — Bottle Tripod Grip — Pen Static Power Hold — Phone The phone is lifted and held using a power grasp without thumb interaction Precision Pinch — Paper / Coin Lateral Pinch — Book Each grip is performed in a structured sequence within a session. Recording Protocol Each session follows a predefined sequence: Phase Action Duration Grip 1 Bottle (Power grasp) 5 s Transition Relax 2 s Grip 2 Pen (Tripod) 5 s Transition Relax 2 s Grip 3 Phone (Static hold) 5 s Transition Relax 2 s Grip 4 Paper/Coin (Pinch) 5 s Transition Relax 2 s Grip 5 Book (Lateral pinch) 5 s This structure enables: Clear segmentation Temporal modeling Transition analysis between grips Sampling and Format Sampling rate: ~30 FPS Units: Degrees Data format: Excel (.xlsx) Visualization: Session-wise trajectory plots (.png) Each Excel file contains: A Data sheet with time-series joint angles and annotations A Metadata sheet with session-level information Processing Pipeline Capture video frames from webcam Detect hand landmarks using MediaPipe Hands Compute joint angles using vector geometry Record continuous time-series data Annotate trials and grip transitions Store structured data in Excel format Generate visualization plots for analysis Key Contributions Continuous session-level dataset (rare in existing literature) Temporal annotations (Trial_ID, Grip_ID) Real-time capture setup (no specialized hardware) Joint angle representation (compact and interpretable) Suitable for both AI research and biomechanical analysis Potential Applications This dataset can be used for: Time-series forecasting (LSTM, GRU, Transformers) Hand gesture and grasp classification Human-computer interaction (HCI) systems Biomechanical analysis of hand motion Rehabilitation and assistive technologies Motion prediction and sequence modeling Limitations Limited to right-handed subjects Captured using a single RGB camera (no depth sensor) Possible noise due to landmark estimation errors Controlled environment (not fully unconstrained real-world settings) Future Work Inclusion of left-handed subjects Multi-view or depth-based recordings Higher sampling rates Expanded activity set Integration with force or EMG data Author and Acknowledgment candidates.title: Dataset for Evaluating Accuracy and Runtime Trade-Offs of Simulation-Based Virtual Sensors
candidates.description: This dataset provides benchmark data for the evaluation of simulation-based virtual sensors in mechanical engineering. It supports the analysis of accuracy, runtime behavior, and deployment trade-offs for physics-based virtual sensing workflows. The dataset includes processed and derived results from two representative case studies: (A) a nonlinear tension-bar benchmark and (B) a steady-state thermal model of a multi-core CPU. The data cover live finite element virtual sensors (SVS-LFE) as well as lookup-database virtual sensors (SVS-LDB) constructed using different design-of-experiments strategies and database sizes. For both case studies, the dataset contains accuracy metrics, runtime measurements, mesh convergence results, lookup-database design data, and aggregated comparison tables. The data enable verification of the quantitative results reported in the accompanying publication and provide a reference for future method development and benchmarking. The repository contains processed numerical data only. Full finite element models, meshes, solver input files, and proprietary software outputs are not included.

candidates.title: ME-AD: Progressive Robotics Anomaly Detection Dataset
candidates.description: Introduction The ME-AD (Mitsubishi Electric Anomaly Detection) dataset contains operating data of cyclic pick-and-place executions collected from a 6-DoF Mitsubishi Electric RV-7FM-D1-S15 manipulator under progressive actuation degradation. A defect was intentionally introduced in the actuator of joint 3 (removal of gearbox lubricant), causing gradual mechanical wear over pick-and-place cycles. Unlike existing robotics AD datasets where anomalies are artificially induced, ME-AD documents an actual progressive hardware fault, making it uniquely suited for benchmarking semi-supervised anomaly detection, online/early fault detection, and remaining useful life estimation. At a Glance The size of the unzipped dataset is ~10GB. The dataset contains approximately 17,000 pick-and-place cycles organized into 7 operation groups called tasks across 3 motion families. Each cycle includes joint positions, velocities, accelerations, and torques sampled at ~280 Hz. The dataset provides raw CSV files, cleaned Pandas DataFrames (.pkl), and pre-configured AD task splits. Each data sample contains 6 joint positions (rad), 6 joint velocities (rad/s), 6 joint accelerations (rad/s²), and 6 joint torques (Nm). Processed files include both raw and low-pass filtered signals. ME-AD/ contains: CSV/ (raw per-cycle CSV files organized by operation code), Pandas/ (cleaned .pkl DataFrames per cycle), Tasks/ (7 pre-configured AD benchmark tasks with training/healthy/faulty splits), and Python scripts for data processing and task generation. The README.md file contains further details. Citation If you use the ME-AD dataset in your research, please cite our contribution: @article{giacomuzzo2026anomaly, title={Anomaly Detection in Industrial Robotics: A Novel Dataset and Benchmark Method}, author={Giacomuzzo, Giulio and Dalla Libera, Alberto and Arimizu, Daichi and Hachiya, Yuto and Tsuruta, Shinya and Wakimoto, Koji and Kuriyama, Toshiyuki and Romeres, Diego}, journal={}, year={2026} } License The ME-AD dataset is released under CC-BY-SA-4.0 license. candidates.title: Multimodal Reclaimed Timber Dataset: X-ray CT Volumes, Visual Grading, Dynamic Tests, Mechanical Tests, and Finite Element and Continuum Model Results with Density, Fibre Orientation and Stiffness Fields
candidates.description: The dataset accompanies the publication:Huber, J.A.J., Svilans, T., Kauniste, M. et al. Comparative evaluation of non-destructive and CT-derived indicators for stiffness assessment of reclaimed Norway spruce timber. Eur. J. Wood Prod. 84, 81 (2026). DOI: 10.1007/s00107-026-02433-1 This dataset provides a comprehensive multimodal characterisation of 56 reclaimed structural timber elements, combining X-ray computed tomography (CT), visual grading, dynamic excitation, mechanical bending tests, and computational modelling. It enables reproducible research in non-destructive evaluation, structural timber assessment, digital twins, and computational wood mechanics. Contents The dataset includes (check README.md for more details): X-ray CT volumes (CT-volumes/) Reconstructed 16-bit greyscale volumes in NRRD format, acquired with a Microtec Mito industrial CT system at 0.5 mm voxel size. Headers include full spatial metadata (spacing, orientation, axes). The scans capture knots, fissures, voids, wane, and other reclaimed-timber features. Loadable with ParaView, ITK/SimpleITK, 3D Slicer, PyVista, and pynrrd. Continuum-mechanics (CM) models (CM-models/) Voxel-based VTK image files (.vti) containing density, binary masks, and orthotropic stiffness fields (Eₓ, Gₓᵧ, Gₓ𝑧) derived from CT. Finite element (FE) models (FE-models/) CalculiX output files (.frd, .dat), Paraview-ready unstructured grids (.vtu), and tessellated surface meshes (.stl). Fields include global and local stresses/strains, displacement fields, fibre-orientation vectors, and results from bending and modal analyses. Profile-level datasets (profiles/) HDF5 files with CT-, CM-, and FE-derived scalar and profile quantities; longitudinal stiffness profiles; bending MOE profiles for 0° (strong-axis) and 90° (weak-axis) bending; equivalent moduli; geometric properties; and full centreline analysis.Additional directories provide CM and FE profile plots along each beam. Statistical analyses (statistics/) Correlation heatmaps, regression performance metrics (R², RMSE, MAE), correlation metrics, pairwise comparison grids, and distribution plots for density, MC, MOE, and visual grading. Includes both zone-wise and beam-wise analyses. Summary table (result_summary.csv) Unified zone-wise and beam-wise dataset containing all experimental, dynamic, CM-derived, FE-derived, and grading indicators. Includes consistent variable naming conventions (e.g., CM_*, FE_*, TNO_*) and statistical aggregates (_zonemean, _beammax, etc.). Example visualisations Images illustrating the FE mesh, coordinate systems, fibre-direction fields, and transverse stress distributions. Relevance This dataset offers: High-resolution structural and material fields for irregular, defect-rich reclaimed timber Integrated multimodal measurements for benchmarking NDT methods Reproducible FE and CM modelling workflows based on CT-derived orthotropic fields Full statistical evaluation resources for comparative or machine-learning studies Extensibility for future work on digital twins / digital shadows, grading optimisation, and reuse assessment It is intended to support researchers in wood science, structural engineering, computational mechanics, image-based modelling, and circular construction.

candidates.title: New datasets obtained from experimental installations with centralized control
candidates.description: The dataset contains the data that local controller 1 (LC1) received from local controller 2 (LC2) during normal system operation. The system was created and it is located in the Laboratory for Manufacturing Automation at the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Belgrade. The system is based on a smart sensor (electromagnetic linear encoder with local controller) and a smart actuator (rodless pneumatic cylinder with electro-pneumatic pressure regulator and local controller), and the main goal is to achieve the desired position of the piston on the pneumatic cylinder. The dataset includes 7 signals that represent a combination of different piston trajectories. Each signal was recorded during the 200 minutes of piston movement along a defined trajectory, where the length of each signal is 400,000 samples. Table 2 shows the list of collected signals, whereas a detailed description of the system can be found in [1]. This dataset was developed with the support of the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia, Grant No. 6523109, AI - MISSION4.0, 2020-2022.

candidates.title: OV3660 Image Dataset of Humans, Dogs and Cats for Neural Network Development in a Teleoperated Rescue Robot
candidates.description: Descripción del conjunto de datos Español Descripción y objetivo Este conjunto de datos forma parte de una investigación desarrollada en la Universidad de Pamplona, Colombia, orientada al diseño de un vehículo terrestre teleoperado para apoyar actividades de búsqueda y rescate en entornos de difícil acceso. El conjunto contiene imágenes de personas, perros y gatos, capturadas mediante una cámara OmniVision OV3660 con lente de campo de visión de 120°, integrada en un módulo ESP32-S3-CAM instalado en el vehículo. Su propósito es verificar la adquisición y entrada de datos visuales, así como proporcionar muestras para preparar el entrenamiento de una red neuronal destinada a la identificación de personas y animales. Arquitectura del sistema El vehículo utiliza dos orugas triangulares independientes, accionadas por motorreductores de corriente continua con encoders Hall. El sistema de control integra un ESP32-S3, comunicación inalámbrica WiFi y una interfaz de supervisión desarrollada en NI LabVIEW. La regulación de velocidad se basa en un controlador proporcional-integral difuso de tipo 2, con inferencia Takagi–Sugeno y una estructura de nueve reglas, de acuerdo con la configuración actual del proyecto. El sistema de percepción combina la cámara OV3660 para adquisición de imágenes visibles y un sensor térmico AMG8833 de 8 × 8 elementos para visualizar distribuciones de temperatura. Aplicación y alcance Las imágenes se utilizarán para evaluar el flujo de adquisición de información visual, organizar las muestras en tres categorías y preparar los procedimientos de entrenamiento y evaluación de una red neuronal. La captura con el mismo hardware utilizado en el vehículo permite disponer de imágenes representativas de su sistema de adquisición. Esto facilita el desarrollo de futuras funciones de reconocimiento visual integradas en la plataforma robótica. El conjunto corresponde a una etapa experimental preliminar. Por tanto, no constituye todavía una validación del desempeño de la red neuronal ni de la detección automática de víctimas en escenarios reales. Institución: Universidad de Pamplona, Colombia. Año: 2026. Áreas de investigación: Ingeniería Mecatrónica, Robótica Móvil, Visión por Computador, Redes Neuronales y Control Inteligente. English Dataset Description and Objectives This dataset is part of a research project developed at Universidad de Pamplona, Colombia, focused on a teleoperated ground robot designed to support search-and-rescue operations in challenging environments. The dataset contains images of humans, dogs, and cats captured using an OmniVision OV3660 camera equipped with a 120° field-of-view lens and integrated into an onboard ESP32-S3-CAM module. Its purpose is to evaluate visual data acquisition and input processing while providing image samples for preparing the training of a neural network intended for human and animal recognition. System Architecture The robotic platform employs two independently driven triangular tracks, DC gear motors with Hall encoders, an ESP32-S3 microcontroller, WiFi communication, and a LabVIEW-based supervisory interface. According to the current project configuration, speed regulation is performed using a type-2 Takagi–Sugeno fuzzy proportional-integral controller incorporating nine inference rules. The perception system combines an OV3660 visible-light camera and an AMG8833 infrared thermal sensor with an 8 × 8 sensing array. Applications and Scope The collected images are intended to support visual data acquisition testing, organization into three semantic categories, and preparation for subsequent neural network training and evaluation. Acquiring images with the robotic platform's own camera provides data representative of its visual sensing configuration, supporting the development of future onboard recognition capabilities. This dataset represents a preliminary experimental stage and does not yet establish validated neural network performance or reliable victim detection under real disaster conditions. Institution: Universidad de Pamplona, Colombia. Year: 2026. Research Areas: Mechatronics Engineering, Mobile Robotics, Computer Vision, Neural Networks, and Intelligent Control.

English Dataset Description and Objectives This dataset is part of a research project developed at Universidad de Pamplona, Colombia, focused on a teleoperated ground robot designed to support search-and-rescue operations in challenging environments. The dataset contains images of humans, dogs, and cats captured using an OmniVision OV3660 camera equipped with a 120° field-of-view lens and integrated into an onboard ESP32-S3-CAM module. Its purpose is to evaluate visual data acquisition and input processing while providing image samples for preparing the training of a neural network intended for human and animal recognition. Applications and Scope The collected images are intended to support visual data acquisition testing, organization into three semantic categories, and preparation for subsequent neural network training and evaluation. Acquiring images with the robotic platform's own camera provides data representative of its visual sensing configuration, supporting the development of future onboard recognition capabilities. This dataset represents a preliminary experimental stage and does not yet establish validated neural network performance or reliable victim detection under real disaster conditions. candidates.title: SubPipe: A Submarine Pipeline Inspection Dataset for Segmentation and Visual-inertial Localization
candidates.description: Abstract This paper presents SubPipe, an underwater dataset for SLAM, object detection, and image segmentation. SubPipe has been recorded using a lightweight autonomous underwater vehicle (LAUV), operated by OceanScan MST, and carrying a sensor suite including two cameras, a side-scan sonar, and an inertial navigation system, among other sensors. The AUV has been deployed in a pipeline inspection environment with a submarine pipe partially covered by sand. The AUV's pose ground truth is estimated from the navigation sensors. The side-scan sonar and RGB images include object detection and segmentation annotations, respectively. State-of-the-art segmentation, object detection, and SLAM methods are benchmarked on SubPipe to demonstrate the dataset's challenges and opportunities for leveraging computer vision algorithms. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first annotated underwater dataset providing a real pipeline inspection scenario. The dataset and experiments are publicly available online. On Zenodo we provide three versions for SubPipe. One is the full version ( SubPipe.zip , ~80GB unzipped) and two subsamples: SubPipeMini.zip , ~12GB unzipped and SubPipeMini2.zip , ~16GB unzipped. Both subsamples are only parts of the entire dataset (SubPipe.zip). SubPipeMini is a subset, containing semantic segmentation data, and it has interesting camera data of the underwater pipeline. On the other hand, SubPipeMini2 is mainly focused on underwater side-scan sonar images of the seabed including ground truth object detection bounding boxes of the pipeline. For (re-)using/publishing SubPipe, please include the following copyright text: SubPipe is a public dataset of a submarine outfall pipeline, property of Oceanscan-MST. This dataset was acquired with a Light Autonomous Underwater Vehicle by Oceanscan-MST, within the scope of Challenge Camp 1 of the H2020 REMARO project. candidates.title: A multimodal inertial sensing and wearable video dataset for human locomotion across terrains and speeds
candidates.description: Human locomotion changes with terrain, walking speed, and transitions between surfaces, yet few public datasets combine bilateral lower-limb inertial sensing with wearable video and third-person camera recordings across natural walking environments. We present the Gait-Terrain Multimodal Dataset (GMT-15), a synchronized multimodal dataset collected from 15 adults performing locomotion tasks on stairs, concrete, grass, sand, gravel, and inclined surfaces. Each participant wore four inertial measurement units (IMUs) attached to the left shank, right shank, left foot, and right foot, respectively. In addition, two wearable cameras were used to capture synchronized video recordings: one mounted on the chest and the other on the shank. The dataset also includes representative third-person camera recordings to provide an external visual perspective of participants' locomotion and surrounding terrain conditions. Participants completed 16 steady-terrain and/or terrain-transition conditions at self-selected slow, preferred, and fast walking speeds, with two repetitions per condition. The released resource contains raw and processed inertial signals, synchronized wearable camera videos, representative third-person camera recordings, participant and trial metadata, terrain and transition annotations, synchronization records, and quality-control information. Reusable code is provided for data loading, preprocessing, visualization, participant-independent data partitioning, and baseline terrain and transition recognition. The dataset supports research in multimodal locomotion recognition, wearable robotics, prosthetic and exoskeleton control, and terrain-adaptive assistance.

candidates.description: This dataset includes experimental data generated during a doctoral research project focused on polysaccharide-based hydrogels reinforced with cellulose nanocrystals (CNC) for extrusion-based 3D bioprinting applications aimed at cartilage tissue engineering. candidates.title: The Collective Rider System (CRS) — Autonomous DSR/X Retrofit & CRS-A1 Production Platform
candidates.description: The Collective Rider System (CRS) — Autonomous DSR/X Retrofit & CRS-A1 Production Platform 1. Executive Summary 1.1. The Purpose of This Paper This document serves as the definitive architectural blueprint and strategic proposal for the Collective Rider System (CRS), a unified autonomous mobility platform designed to bridge the schism between current electric motorcycle capability and a future of fully autonomous, AI-native, self-healing robotic vehicles. The scope of this paper is exhaustive, covering the mechanical, computational, and governance layers required to deliver two distinct but sequentially linked hardware deliverables: the CRS–DSRX Retrofit Prototype (based on the 2026 Zero DSR/X) and the CRS-A1 Production Model (a clean-sheet design for 2027/28). We currently stand at a unique inflection point in the trajectory of personal mobility. While electrification has become standardized—evidenced by the maturity of the Zero Motorcycles Z-Force powertrain—true autonomy in single-track vehicles (motorcycles) lags significantly behind four-wheeled counterparts. This lag is not a failure of ambition but a consequence of physics: a motorcycle must balance before it can navigate. The "inverted pendulum" problem requires control loops with latency tolerances an order of magnitude tighter than those required for a stable four-wheeled chassis. Current market solutions, such as Honda’s Riding Assist, have demonstrated the viability of steer-by-wire and geometry modification for low-speed balance 1, yet no production-ready system exists that integrates high-speed autonomy, predictive energy health, and heavy-payload logistics into a single, commercially viable platform. The CRS fills this void. It is not merely a self-driving feature set; it is a holistic operating system for the machine, governing its physics, its energy chemistry, and its decision-making via the CollectiveOS framework.2 This paper outlines how we will leverage the industry-leading chassis of the Zero DSR/X, the supercomputing edge power of Intel’s Agilex/Arc silicon 3, the visual perception of GoPro’s GP2/GP3 architecture 5, and the cloud-training infrastructure of Microsoft to create the world’s first "Uncrashable, Unstoppable" robotic motorcycle. 1.2. Vision: The World’s First Fully Autonomous, AI-Native Motorcycle The vision driving the CRS project is the creation of a motorcycle that transcends the limitations of the human rider while preserving the utility and efficiency of the form factor. A motorcycle is inherently more energy-efficient and space-efficient than a car, making it the ideal vector for the next generation of urban logistics, emergency response, and accessible personal transport. However, the skill barrier and safety risks associated with riding limit its adoption. The CRS removes these barriers through active autonomy. The system utilizes a Dual-AI Architecture—comprising the PILOT core for real-time physics and navigation, and the CATALYST core for long-term energy health and system optimization. This allows the machine to: Self-Balance at zero speed without gyroscopes, using steering actuation and geometry modulation derived from Honda’s robotics research.6 Self-Heal its battery chemistry through AI-managed thermal cycles, extending fleet life by 4x.2 Predict collisions before they occur, deploying a "Safety Cocoon" of airbags and evasive maneuvers. Operate Unmanned for logistics and repositioning (Ghost Mode). 1.3. Strategic Deliverables This paper proposes a phased execution strategy to minimize risk while maximizing immediate technological demonstration: CRS–DSRX Retrofit Prototype (2026): A modification package for the existing Zero DSR/X. This leverages Zero’s proven Z-Force 75-10X powertrain and steel trellis frame 7, adding a bolt-on "Supercomputer Sled," a steering actuation module for stability, and an external sensor array. This allows for rapid validation of the software stack and balancing physics without the need for new chassis tooling. CRS-A1 Production Model (2027/28): A native implementation where the compute lattice, sensors, and balancing actuators are integrated into the casting of the frame. The A1 is designed for high-payload utility (300kg+), global fleet homologation, and extended operational life via self-healing capabilities. 1.4. Collaboration Pitch The complexity of this system requires a coalition of best-in-class partners. We position the CRS as a collaborative ecosystem rather than a proprietary walled garden: Zero Motorcycles (OEM Partner): Provides the DSR/X platform, manufacturing capacity, and EV powertrain expertise. candidates.title: AeROpeBOTICS experiments dataset
candidates.description: This flight dataset, provided by the Technical University of Denmark, comes from flight tests performed at the University of Sevilla during the first and second weeks of September 2025, as part of the AeROpeBOTICS project. A Variable Stiffness Link (VSL) is proposed from Technical University of Denmark for long-reach aerial manipulation, enabling adaptable mechanical coupling between an aerial multirotor platform and a dual-arm manipulator provided by University of Sevilla. The proposed VSL introduces an adjustable stiffness mechanism that allows the link to behave either as a flexible rope or as a rigid rod, depending on task requirements. The VSL was tested under external perturbations (impacts, collision, wind) and evaluated its feasibility for package transportation tasks, with and without dual-arms attached. The dataset comprises 3 folders: All bags 7 folders corresponding with 6 days of flight tests plot_data Matlab codes to plot the desired kind of rosbag selected bagg Relevant bags from "All bags" folder. Videos of the relevant experiments - link Folder names decribe the experiment registered in the rosbags they include. candidates.title: Exploratory Topic Modelling in Python Dataset - EHRI-3
candidates.description: In the EHRI-3 project, we are investigating tools and methods that historical researchers and scholars can use to better understand, visualise, and interpret the material held by our partner archives. This dataset accompanies a tutorial exploring a technique called topic modelling in the context of a Holocaust-related historical collection. We were on the lookout for datasets that would be easily accessible and, for convenience, predominantly in English. One such dataset was the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum’s (USHMM) extensive collection of oral history testimonies, for which there are a considerable number of textual transcripts. The museum’s total collection consists of over 80,703 testimonies, 41,695 of which are available in English, with 2,894 of them listing a transcript. Since there is not yet a ready-to-download dataset that includes these transcripts, we had to construct our own. Using a web scraping tool, we managed to create a list of the links pointing to the metadata (including transcripts) of the testimonies that were of interest to us. After obtaining the transcript and other metadata of each of these testimonies, we were able to create our dataset and curate it to remove any unwanted entries. For example, we made sure to remove entries with restrictions on access or use. We also removed entries with transcripts that consisted only of some automatically generated headers and entries which turned out to be in languages other than English. The remaining 1,873 transcripts form the corpus of this tutorial — a small, but still decently sized dataset. The process that we followed to put together this dataset is detailed in the Jupyter Notebook accompanying this post, which can be found in this Github repository . In this Zenodo upload, the user can find two files, each of them containing a pickled pandas DataFrame that was obtained at a different stage of the tutorial: "unrestricted_df.pkl" contains 1,946 entries of Oral Testimony transcripts and has five fields (RG_number, text, display_date, conditions_access, conditions_use) "unrestricted_lemmatized_df.pkl" contains 1,873 entries of Oral Testimony transcripts and has six fields (RG_number, text, display_date, conditions_access, conditions_use, lemmas) Instructions on their intended use can be found in the accompanying Jupyter Notebook. Credits: The transcripts that form the corpus in this tutorial were obtained through the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum (USHMM).

candidates.title: INTELLIGENT SOLUTIONS AND MACHINE LEARNING IN MECHANICAL ENGINEERING: APPLICATION OPPORTUNITIES AND PROMISING DIRECTIONS
candidates.description: This article analyzes the current state, practical applications, and promising development directions of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) technologies in mechanical engineering. The study examines the application of AI and ML methods in predictive maintenance, design optimization, manufacturing and process optimization, robotics and automation, quality control, and structural health monitoring. The capabilities of modern approaches, including neural networks, deep learning, reinforcement learning, transfer learning, and Bayesian optimization, in solving complex engineering problems are also discussed. Particular attention is paid to the integration of data-driven models with physics-based models, uncertainty quantification, model interpretability, reliability, and adaptability under different operating conditions. The analysis demonstrates that the integration of AI and ML into mechanical engineering provides significant opportunities for improving production efficiency, reducing maintenance costs, enhancing product quality, optimizing engineering processes, and developing sustainable engineering solutions. The study also identifies promising research directions related to physics-informed artificial intelligence, explainable AI, uncertainty-aware models, hybrid intelligent systems, and adaptive engineering technologies.

candidates.title: Multimodal Terrestrial Cotton Seedling Dataset with Multiview RGB, RealSense Infrared and Depth, Thermal Imaging, and YOLO-Compatible Annotations for Agricultural Row Perception
candidates.description: This dataset contains multimodal terrestrial data of early-stage cotton seedlings collected under real open-field conditions in the Mexicali Valley, Baja California, Mexico. Data were acquired along three field trajectories using a non-motorized terrestrial mobile acquisition platform. The acquisition site is located at 32.569572° N, 115.147613° W. The dataset is intended to support research on crop-row perception, agricultural robotics, multimodal sensing, autonomous navigation, sensor fusion, visual servoing, row-transition analysis, digital twins, and sim-to-real methods for agricultural robotics. The sensing system combined three RGB views; color, depth, and left and right infrared data from an Intel RealSense D435i; thermal measurements from an MLX90640; GPS positioning; inertial measurements; optical-flow and sensor-to-ground distance measurements; and ambient temperature and relative-humidity records. The central RGB camera, Intel RealSense D435i, and thermal sensor were oriented toward the direction of travel, while two lateral RGB cameras provided complementary views of the surrounding crop rows. Field acquisition was conducted under natural daylight between approximately 06:00 and 10:00 h, with both clear and cloudy intervals observed during the acquisition period. The sequences include crop-row tracking, row-end conditions, transitions between adjacent rows, sparse seedling emergence, gaps between plants, exposed soil, weeds, shadows, partial occlusions, and changes in crop-row continuity. These conditions document the visual variability encountered during early-stage cotton-row perception. The dataset is organized into three trajectory-based ZIP archives. Across the three trajectories, the published dataset contains 151,092 files with a combined compressed size of approximately 41.9 GB. These files include 149,769 images, 306 videos, and 383 CSV files, together with metadata, YOLO labels, documentation, configuration files, and supporting Python code. Trajectory 1 contains 39,122 files, including 38,652 images, 108 videos, and 131 CSV files, with a compressed size of approximately 8.8 GB. Trajectory 2 contains 34,219 files, including 33,742 images, 126 videos, and 137 CSV files, with a compressed size of approximately 8.9 GB. Trajectory 3 contains 77,751 files, including 77,375 images, 72 videos, and 115 CSV files, with a compressed size of approximately 24.2 GB. Each trajectory follows the same general directory organization, separating original acquisitions, modality-specific data, processed data, derived products, annotations, article-supporting tables and figures, documentation, and software resources. The main directories include raw/, organized/, processed/, derived/, annotations/, article_tables/, article_figures/, docs/, and code/. A master_index.csv file included with each trajectory provides a general reference for locating files according to sensing modality, file location, and processing level. File names retain acquisition identifiers, dates, times, and sensing modalities. Prefixes such as IMGSET, THSET, RSDSET, and VIDSET identify image acquisitions, thermal acquisitions, RealSense acquisitions, and video sequences, respectively. This naming convention supports traceability among source acquisitions, processed files, extracted frames, and associated sensor measurements. The visual data include three complementary RGB views: front, left, and right. Each RGB view contains 13,002 images across the three trajectories. Intel RealSense data include 9,768 color images, 9,768 left-infrared images, 9,768 right-infrared images, 9,768 RGB-depth composite images, and 9,736 depth visualizations. The dataset additionally preserves 32 raw Z16 depth captures: 12 from Trajectory 1, 14 from Trajectory 2, and 6 from Trajectory 3. Raw Z16 depth data and depth visualizations should be interpreted as different data products. The depth visualizations are image representations generated from the depth stream for inspection and comparison with the other visual modalities. The raw Z16 captures preserve unsigned 16-bit per-pixel depth values. Their associated metadata include a depth scale of 0.001 m per unit, allowing metric depth to be obtained by multiplying each raw pixel value by this scale. The Intel RealSense metadata also include intrinsic parameters for the color and depth cameras, depth-to-color extrinsic information, and depth-alignment information. These parameters support interpretation of the geometric relationship between the RealSense color and depth streams. Thermal data were acquired with an MLX90640 sensor. The sensor produces native 32 × 24 temperature matrices describing the spatial distribution of temperature across the observed scene. The dataset includes 12,357 thermal visualizations at 640 × 480 pixels. These visualizations provide an image-like representation for comparison with the other sensing modalities and should not be interpreted as the native spatial resolution of the thermal sensor. The visual data are accompanied by navigation, motion, optical-flow, distance, and environmental measurements. GPS records include latitude, longitude, altitude, cumulative distance, speed, satellite information, HDOP, and Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). Inertial measurements include acceleration, angular velocity, magnetometer measurements, and orientation estimates. The MTF-01 provides optical-flow information, signal-quality or strength measurements, and sensor-to-ground distance. Ambient temperature and relative humidity were recorded using a DHT11 sensor. The visual streams and sensor measurements were acquired through independent software-controlled acquisition cycles. Files and measurements belonging to the same acquisition event are associated through common acquisition identifiers and software-recorded timestamps. The variable pc_time corresponds to the host-computer local clock, whereas gps_time_utc corresponds to UTC obtained from the GPS receiver. The sensing modalities were not recorded using a shared hardware trigger; therefore, temporal relationships should be interpreted using the acquisition identifiers, timestamps, and metadata provided with the dataset. Extracted video frames retain information linking them to their source videos. The frame_manifest.csv files associate extracted images with their source video, frame number, timestamp, original frame rate, total number of source frames, and extraction interval. Together with master_index.csv and the common acquisition identifiers, these files support navigation and traceability throughout the dataset. The dataset also includes YOLO annotations for segmentation, oriented bounding boxes (OBBs), and pose. The annotations cover 210 different source images from the three field trajectories: 75 from Trajectory 1, 57 from Trajectory 2, and 78 from Trajectory 3. By visual modality, the annotated images comprise 51 RGB images, 51 RealSense infrared images, 52 depth or RGB-depth images, and 56 thermal images. Some source images are used in more than one annotation task. Consequently, the annotation exports contain 339 task-level image-label pairs: 122 for segmentation, 152 for oriented bounding boxes, and 65 for pose. Across all supported annotation tasks, the YOLO label files contain 1,678 individual annotation entries. The annotations are organized by visual modality within the annotations/ directory, with separate groups for RGB, RealSense infrared, depth or RGB-depth, and thermal data. Within these modality groups, the available annotation tasks are organized as yolo_seg/, yolo_obb/, and yolo_pose/. The corresponding directories contain the images, label files, and data.yaml configuration files required to interpret the YOLO annotations. The class names remain in Spanish as defined in the corresponding data.yaml files. These include hilera (crop row), surco (furrow), maleza (weed), and suelo (soil). In the pose annotations, the crop-row class is represented as HILERA. The lowercase and uppercase forms refer to the same crop-row concept and reflect the nomenclature retained for the corresponding annotation task. The three annotation types represent complementary descriptions of crop-row geometry. Segmentation annotations delineate visible regions of interest. OBB annotations describe the position, orientation, and spatial extent of row-related structures. Pose annotations use five ordered keypoints distributed along the visible crop row to represent its geometry. The first keypoint identifies the near portion of the visible row and the fifth keypoint identifies its farther visible extent, while the intermediate points describe the continuity and geometry of the row between these positions. The repository also includes variable dictionaries, sensor tables, navigation records, annotation information, file indexes, quality-control information, documentation, and software used for acquisition, organization, post-processing, inspection, and dataset preparation. These supporting resources are intended to facilitate interpretation of the published files and reproducible reuse of the multimodal records. Final data-quality checks covered file readability, consistency of file names and paths, availability of the expected sensing modalities, integrity of navigation, inertial, RealSense, thermal, and environmental tables, and correspondence between annotated images and their YOLO label files. The dataset can be reused for research on agricultural robotics, crop-row perception, crop-row detection and tracking, row-center estimation, visual guidance and control, RGB-D analysis, infrared and thermal field inspection, multimodal perception, visual-inertial analysis, sensor fusion, temporal data association, digital twins, sim-to-real methods, dataset curation, and the development or evaluation of YOLO-compatible perception methods for field agricultural robots. Important limitations should be considered when reusing the dataset. Association among sensing modalities is based on common acquisition identifiers and software timestamps rather than a shared hardware trigger. GPS positions were acquired without Real-Time Kinematic (RTK) correction.

candidates.title: Research dataset for the validation of the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) among secondary school teachers in Greece
candidates.description: This dataset supports the study on the validation of a Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) instrument among Greek secondary school teachers. It includes anonymized data collected from teachers in secondary education in Greece. The dataset contains responses to items measuring the main TAM constructs, including Perceived Ease of Use (PEOU), Perceived Usefulness (PU), adapted Perceived Usefulness items (NPU), and Behavioral Intention (BI), as well as demographic and professional background variables. In addition to the raw variables, the dataset includes recoded variables used in multi-group analyses, such as gender, teaching subject area, diploma level, school type, age group, and teaching years. A codebook is provided to explain the coding scheme and the recoding procedures. These data were used for exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, exploratory graph analysis, measurement invariance testing, and structural model evaluation. All data have been anonymized prior to publication.

candidates.title: XJTU-DV: Open-Source Dynamic Vision Dataset for Non-Contact Vibration Measurement and Fault Diagnosis of Mechanical Systems
candidates.description: XJTU-DV, an open-source dynamic vision dataset for non-contact vibration measurement and fault diagnosis of mechanical systems. The XJTU-DV-Beam sub-dataset includes the dynamic vision data on a structural beam system, as well as the corresponding laser vibrometer data as ground truths. The XJTU-DV-Rotor and XJTU-DV-Pump sub-datasets include the dynamic vision data from a rotor and a pump test bench, respectively. The dynamic vision data are collected under different fault and operating conditions. XJTU-DV provides a data foundation for dynamic vision-based studies on vibration measurement and fault diagnosis, which may promote further development of the emerging vision algorithms for industrial applications. The dataset can be accessed with the link https://gr.xjtu.edu.cn/web/lixiang/xjtu-dv For more detailed dataset information, please refer to: Xiang Li, Shupeng Yu, Xinrui Chen, Yaguo Lei, Bin Yang*, Naipeng Li, XJTU-DV: Open-Source Dynamic Vision Dataset for Non-Contact Vibration Measurement and Fault Diagnosis of Mechanical Systems , Chinese Journal of Mechanical Engineering, 2026 If XJTU-DV data are used in your research, it is requested to cite the references: Xiang Li, Shupeng Yu, Yaguo Lei, Naipeng Li, Bin Yang*, " Dynamic Vision-Based Machinery Fault Diagnosis With Cross-Modality Feature Alignment ", IEEE/CAA Journal of Automatica Sinica, 2024, 11(10), 2068–2081. If you have any questions regarding the dataset, please contact Xiang Li through Email lixiang@xjtu.edu.cn

candidates.title: A Unified Framework for Soft Robotics (2025–2040): Integrating Materials, Modeling, AI-Driven Control, Fabrication Pipelines, and Global Ethical Governance
candidates.description: 📌 Title A Unified Framework for Soft Robotics (2025–2040): Integrating Materials, Modeling, AI-Driven Control, Fabrication Pipelines, and Global Ethical Governance --- 📌 Description / Abstract (for Zenodo entry) This research presents a comprehensive and interdisciplinary framework for advancing soft robotics from fragmented laboratory prototypes toward globally scalable, reproducible, and ethically governed technologies. Bridging materials science, continuum modeling, artificial intelligence, fabrication engineering, and policy foresight, the study proposes a unified pipeline that directly addresses reproducibility deficits, scalability bottlenecks, and regulatory blind spots in the field. The framework integrates standardized benchmarking of elastomers, hydrogels, dielectric actuators, biodegradable composites, and shape-memory systems; advanced constitutive and continuum models (Kelvin–Voigt, Ogden, Cosserat rods) coupled with digital twins and uncertainty quantification; hybrid AI–physics control architectures combining model predictive control (MPC) and reinforcement learning (RL); and scalable fabrication pipelines encompassing mold casting, lithography, DIW printing, and hybrid manufacturing. Validation protocols employ ANOVA, Weibull reliability analysis, power statistics, and pre-registered open datasets, ensuring transparent reproducibility. Ethical and governance dimensions align with FDA, EU MDR, ISO standards, and the UN Sustainable Development Goals, while proposing an International Soft Robotics Governance Council (ISRGC). The roadmap (2025–2040) defines three phases—Consolidation, Expansion, and Maturity—marking the transition of soft robotics into medicine, sustainable environmental systems, and adaptive industrial automation. By merging technical innovation with normative responsibility, this work positions soft robotics as a 21st-century socio-technological pillar for safe, inclusive, and sustainable human progress. --- 📌 Author & Affiliation Author: B. candidates.title: A Unified Framework for Soft Robotics: Materials, Modeling, AI-Driven Control, Fabrication, and Global Policy Standards (2025–2040)
candidates.description: Title A Comprehensive Unified Framework for Soft Robotics: Advanced Materials, Continuum Modeling, Hybrid AI Control, Fabrication Techniques, and Global Governance Standards (2025–2040) Description (Abstract) This thesis proposes a groundbreaking and integrative framework for soft robotics research and application, overcoming the existing fragmentation across multi-disciplinary domains including advanced materials, continuum mechanics, AI-driven control systems, scalable fabrication technologies, and ethical global policy frameworks. It systematically evaluates elastomers, hydrogels, dielectric actuators, shape-memory materials, and biodegradable composite polymers under rigorous benchmarking protocols focused on mechanical performance, biocompatibility, and sustainability. Advanced modeling integrates Kelvin–Voigt viscoelasticity, Ogden hyperelasticity, and Cosserat rod theories, enhanced through probabilistic reliability assessments and digital twin simulations for real-time prediction and control. The novel hybrid AI-physics control approach, combining model predictive control with reinforcement learning and explainable AI frameworks, ensures adaptable, safe, and interpretable autonomous soft robotic operations. Comparative studies of fabrication pipelines—including mold casting, soft lithography, direct ink writing, and hybrid additive manufacturing—highlight trade-offs between cost-efficiency, reproducibility, scalability, and environmental impact. An innovative governance blueprint aligns with FDA, EU MDR, ISO standards, and UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), proposing the establishment of an International Soft Robotics Governance Council (ISRGC) to harmonize global standards. Validated by multidisciplinary case studies spanning clinical tools, eco-monitoring, and industrial automation, this work sets a new global benchmark for reproducible, ethical, and sustainable soft robotics technology deployment up to 2040 and beyond. Keywords Soft robotics; viscoelastic and hyperelastic modeling; hybrid AI-physics control architectures; reinforcement learning; model predictive control; materials characterization and benchmarking; digital twin simulations; advanced fabrication pipelines; reproducibility and scalability; uncertainty quantification; regulatory compliance (FDA, EU MDR); ISO international standards; governance and ethics in robotics; sustainable and biodegradable materials; interdisciplinary integration; open science protocols; global soft robotics roadmap 2025–2040.

candidates.title: AI Regulation Media Texts Dataset: Comparable Corpora in Czech and Portuguese (2018-2023)
candidates.description: AI Regulation Media Texts Dataset: Comparable Corpora in Czech and Portuguese (2018-2023) is a collection of online mainstream news articles on Artificial Intelligence (AI) regulation in the European Union context. It consists of texts between 2018 and 2023, focusing on Czech and Portuguese media outlets. For analytical purposes, the dataset comprises two comparable textual corpora (texts on a given topic, from a given period, and representing a specific part of the media sector), one for each country in the given language. The dataset was collected as part of the project CORRELATE – Corpora and Lexical and Terminological Resources ( https://clunl.fcsh.unl.pt/en/projetos/projetos-curso/correlate-corpora-e-recursos-lexicais-e-terminologicos/ ). The data was collected through a combination of downloading from the paid media database Annopress (Czech corpus) and web scraping, using BootCat 1.57 (Portuguese corpus). Considering this, the data is available solely for further academic and scientific use (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0). The search was based on the common seed terms related to “artificial intelligence” and “EU regulation”, or the specific title of the EU’s “AI Act” document, including synonyms and different clusters, in each language. Specific mainstream online media outlets were selected, as classified by NFNZ and Netmonitor for Czechia (22 media outlets) and by Netaudience and Clube de Imprensa for Portugal (32 media outlets), and published between March 2018 and December 2023. This period is defined by the establishment of the first AI expert group and the European AI alliance in 2018, and the final political agreement on the “AI Act” regulation in 2023. The Czech corpus consists of 659,388 tokens, distributed across 675 articles, from March 2018 until December 2023. The Portuguese corpus covers the same time periods and comprises 539,199 tokens, distributed across 361 articles. The corpora were cleaned of duplicates (based on URL, text content, and title) and shallow-processed (tokenisation, lemmatisation, and POS tagging) using Sketch Engine software. Enabling more nuanced analysis, the corpora also include the following metadata: source/medium, author, publication year, URL. Both resulting corpora are available in two formats: plain text (.txt) and shallow-processed vertical file or word-per-line format (.vert), useful for further linguistic corpus analysis. candidates.title: ChildSafeLLM: A Dataset of Child Safety Aligned Evaluation Prompts for Generative AIs
candidates.description: ChildSafeLLM (Child Safety Aligned Evaluation Prompts for Generative AIs) is a developmental benchmark comprising 200 total prompts carefully crafted and curated for two distinct age cohorts—ages 6-12 and ages 7-13. Drawing on evidence-based child-safety guidelines, school curricula, and authentic questions from children and caregivers, the prompts were sourced from reputable organizations across six continents to ensure broad cultural and linguistic representation. Available in .xlsx, ChildSafeLLM supports a wide range of natural-language processing tasks, including harmful-content detection, age-appropriateness classification, response-consistency analysis, safety-alignment fine-tuning, and developmental language modeling. Beyond its use for model training, the corpus offers a reproducible benchmark for evaluating ambiguity resolution, risk-category labeling, and multi-turn dialogue safety in child–AI interactions. By standardizing safety scenarios for younger users, ChildSafeLLM advances research into trustworthy AI design and helps practitioners assess how generative models accommodate children’s cognitive and emotional needs. candidates.title: Dataset for quantification of CFUs using AI
candidates.description: In recent years, smartphones and software have developed to help to automate imaging processes and thereby support digitalization in clinical microbiology laboratories. Due to the time-consuming nature of manual bacterial colony counting, diverse apps for smartphones have been developed to quantify the number of colony-forming units (CFUs) on agar plate images. Currently, at least four different apps with a colony counter function exist. Our study aimed to compare the accuracy of the apps compared to human visual manual counting. The images were acquired using four different colony counters with three apps on an iPhone 11 Pro Max (CFU.Ai, Promega Colony Counter, APD Colony Counter App PRO) and one app on a Samsung Galaxy A52 (@BactLAB). Two different measurement conditions were investigated. Firstly, standardized measurement in a handcrafted wooden apparatus, and secondly “freestyle measurement” manually holding the plate. The apparatus measurements were performed against a black background, apart from @BactLAB on a white background (as per the manufacturer’s instructions). We used three different types of media: blood agar, chrome agar, and LB. Four Escherichia coli isolates were used. We prepared a bacterial suspension of each strain, made a six-fold serial 1:10 dilution in saline and spread the dilutions “1:10 4 ”, “1:10 5 ”, and “1:10 6 ” at three different solution volumes (100 μ l , 50 μ l , and 25 μ l) homogeneously across the agar plates. We included a total of 108 agar plates. This dataset contains all analyzed images. It may possibly be useful in order to assess and improve colony counter apps in the future. On the one hand, the dataset contains raw data (images before processing), on the other hand, it contains screenshots of our app measurement and thus enables accountability of our results (screenshots of all apps were uploaded apart from @BactLAB as from its screenshots nothing can be derived).

candidates.title: DUX: A dataset of User Interactions and User Emotions
candidates.description: User experience evaluation is becoming increasingly important, and so is emotion recognition. Recognizing users' emotions based on their interactions alone would not be intrusive to users and could be easily implemented in most applications. This is still an area of active research and requires data containing both the user interactions and the corresponding emotions. Currently, there is no public dataset for emotion recognition from keystroke, mouse and touchscreen dynamics. We have created such a dataset for keyboard and mouse interactions through a dedicated user study and made it publicly available for other researchers. This paper examines our study design and the process of creating the dataset. We conducted the study using a test application for travel expense reports with 50 participants. We want to be able to detect predominantly negative emotions, so we added emotional triggers to our test application. However, further research is needed to determine the relationship between user interactions and emotions.

candidates.title: EMG dataset for gesture recognition with arm translation
candidates.description: Myoelectric control has emerged as a promising approach for a wide range of applications, including controlling limb prosthetics, teleoperating robots, and enabling immersive interactions in the metaverse. However, the accuracy and robustness of myoelectric control systems are often affected by various factors, including muscle fatigue, perspiration, drifts in electrode positions, and changes in arm position. The latter has received less attention despite its significant impact on signal quality and decoding accuracy. To address this gap, we present GREAT, a novel dataset of surface electromyographic (EMG) signals captured from multiple arm positions. This dataset, comprising EMG and hand kinematics data from 8 participants performing 6 different hand gestures, provides a comprehensive resource for investigating position-invariant myoelectric control decoding algorithms. We envision this dataset to serve as a valuable resource for both training and benchmarking arm position-invariant myoelectric control algorithms. Additionally, to further expand the publicly available data capturing the variability of EMG signals across diverse arm positions, we propose a novel data acquisition protocol that can be utilized for future data collection.

candidates.title: Experimental Data for "Enhancing Polymeric Bone Scaffolds Mechanical Characteristics Using Supercritical CO₂ Foaming and Reinforcing Agents"
candidates.description: This dataset contains experimental data supporting the research article "Enhancing Polymeric Bone Scaffolds Mechanical Characteristics Using Supercritical CO₂ Foaming and Reinforcing Agents", published in the Journal of the Taiwan Institute of Chemical Engineers (2024). The study focuses on the development and characterization of porous poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) scaffolds produced using supercritical CO₂ foaming and reinforced with magnesium (Mg), magnesium hydroxide (Mg(OH)₂), and hydroxyapatite (HAp). Reinforcing agents were incorporated into the polymeric matrix through melt extrusion prior to the foaming process. The experimental investigation addresses the influence of processing parameters, particularly pressure and temperature, and reinforcing agents on scaffold morphology, porosity, pore size, and mechanical performance. Characterization techniques include scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), three-dimensional scanning, and compression testing. These data support the analysis of the relationships between processing conditions, scaffold structure, and compressive strength. They are made available to promote transparency, reproducibility, and further research on biodegradable polymeric scaffolds for bone tissue engineering and regenerative medicine.

candidates.title: OSU-Honda automobile hood dataset (CarHoods10k)
candidates.description: The CarHoods10k data set comprises a set of over 10,000 3D mesh geometries for variants of car hood frames, generated through an automated, industry-grade Computer Aided Design (CAD) workflow described in Ramnath (2019). The data set provides realistic designs that were validated by experts with respect to realism, manufacturability, variability, and performance. Variations in geometries were generated by a feature-based approach that varies parameter values describing design features on 109 parameterized base geometries ('skins'). Parameters describe feature patterns such as cut-outs or ribs on the hood frame as well as their properties, for example, rib location and height, or cut-out location. Geometries are represented as surface meshes (STL files) and are provided with the corresponding design parameter values and performance metrics from structural mechanics, generated through finite element analysis (FEA). The data set provides realistic and validated designs for the evaluation and development of methods such as optimization approaches or machine learning for metamodeling or performance prediction. CarHoods10k thus enables the evaluate of data-driven approaches for application in the automotive engineering design domain and others.

candidates.title: High-Throughput Computational Screening and Thermodynamic Benchmarking of 311 Crystalline Candidates and Polymorphs via Autonomous AI and CHGNet
candidates.description: ## Overview (Version 1.1.0 Update)This repository contains the crystallographic structures (`.cif`), quantum-mechanical structural relaxation data, theoretical application dossiers, and thermodynamic phase-stability benchmarks for **311 crystalline solid-state candidates and structural polymorphs** screened computationally. The computational pipeline couples an automated generative LLM exploration engine (constrained by Shannon ionic radii and crystallographic valence balance) with UC Berkeley's **CHGNet** (Crystal Hamiltonian Graph Neural Network) universal potential for quantum structural relaxation, PyMatGen for symmetry and space group classification, and the **Materials Project (MP-API v0.88+)** for thermodynamic convex-hull benchmarking. The repository contains **311 distinct crystalline structures** representing **304 unique chemical stoichiometries** (including 7 distinct structural polymorphs). The thermodynamic phase-stability benchmark categorizes all 304 unique chemical compositions into three synthesis regimes: 47 (Regime 1) + 78 (Regime 2) + 179 (Regime 3) = 304 unique stoichiometries (311 total crystallographic polymorphs). ### Scope and Target Scientific DomainsThe 311 validated candidates span 8 advanced technological domains:1. Ultra-High Temperature Ceramics (UHTCs) & Aerospace Shielding (carbides, nitrides, borides of Hf, Ta, Zr, W, Ti).2. Phase Change Materials (PCMs) & Neuromorphic Computing (chalcogenide architectures with Sb, Bi, Te, Se, In, Sc).3. Quantum Photonics & Non-Linear Optical Crystals (NLO).4. Energy Storage & All-Solid-State Battery Electrolytes (Li, Na, Sc halophosphates and chloro-oxides).5. Unconventional Superconductivity Candidates (low-dimensional chalcogenides and pnictides).6. High-Entropy Alloys (HEAs) with extreme radiation tolerance.7. Quantum 2D Topology & Spintronics.8. Phonon-Engineered Thermoelectrics. ### Validation CriteriaEvery crystal structure in this repository satisfied strict stability and geometric thresholds:- Maximum residual interatomic force: 0 meV/atom).- **Symmetry and Space Group Assignment:** Initial hypotheses were constructed with explicit atomic site coordinates under P1 space group symmetry to avoid crystallographic occupancy collisions during generative AI proposal. Following CHGNet relaxation, structures were analyzed with PyMatGen SpacegroupAnalyzer. While several candidates relaxed into high-symmetry cubic, tetragonal, or orthorhombic space groups (e.g., P6/mmm, Pmmm, C2/m, Cm), candidates retaining P1 symmetry reflect either genuine low-symmetry coordinating networks (common in complex quaternary PCMs and chalcogenides) or sub-angstrom numerical relaxation offsets within the default tolerance (symprec = 0.01 Å). ### Why Metastability Matters in Functional SemiconductorsIn solid-state physics and semiconductor engineering, **thermodynamic ground-state stability (E_hull = 0) is not the sole indicator of functional utility**. Many of the most technologically critical materials—including diamond, wurtzite GaN, phase-change memory alloys (Ge-Sb-Te), halide perovskites (α-CsPbI3), and layered 2D dichalcogenides—are **metastable phases** kinetically trapped under ambient conditions (*Sun et al., Science 2016*). For instance, Phase-Change Materials (PCMs) require low kinetic barriers between metastable crystalline and amorphous phases to enable ultrafast electronic switching. Similarly, narrow-bandgap optoelectronic semiconductors and topological insulators frequently reside in metastable thermodynamic windows readily accessible via non-equilibrium thin-film deposition (MBE, Sputtering, CVD, or Rapid Thermal Annealing). Rather than discarding metastable candidates, **this dataset preserves all 311 materials**, categorizing each candidate into one of three experimentally actionable **Synthesis & Stability Regimes** based on ground-truth data from the **Materials Project**. ### Summary of the Three Synthesis Regimes- **Regime 1: Equilibrium & High-Viability Ground States (E_hull ≤ 50 meV/atom):** **47 materials** (16 on the convex hull + 31 within thermal fluctuation range; synthesizable via standard solid-state reactions and bulk melt cooling).- **Regime 2: Kinetically Trapped Functional Semiconductors (50 150 meV/atom):** **179 materials** (Metastable phases requiring extreme non-equilibrium conditions, diamond anvil cells, or substrate epitaxial pinning). --- ## 1.
